passage:
Mission Statement

As an international primary school, we here at Pinewood Academy give education for boys and girls aged 7-14 before GSCEs. Our sister school, Stirling Contemporary, caters for GSCEs and A-levels. We prioritise bi-lingual learning and offer all of our subjects in both English and French. Our school’s unique approach offers this opportunity to every student at the beginning of Key Stage 2 to the end of Key Stage 3.

Years 2-6 participate in Key Stage 2, and Year 7-9, Key Stage 3. We believe in encompassing a strong communicative approach in line with school policy.

Field Trip A

Pinewood Academy organises a variety of cultural activities throughout the year, starting with our exciting field trips in September and ending with our Spring trip in April. With our focuses on bi-lingual learning, these trips can be a great opportunity to gain first-hand experience of the languages studied at our international school. All field trips will be led and coordinated by their years’ tutor(s). Year 2 & 3 - They will be travelling together as classes for a day trip to Wales. They will be led and coordinated by Mr. Seagull and Mr. Monkman. They will take the Snowdon Railway train to the summit of Snowdonia. Year 4 - They will be travelling for a day trip to the Eden Project in Cornwall.  They will be led and coordinated by Ms. Joseph and Mr. Jason. This trip includes a ride on the Skywire which will be an optional condition as part of the consent form.

Field Trip B

Year 5 - They will be travelling to Budapest from Sept 21-25th. They will be led and coordinated by Ms. Joy and Ms. Ryder. They will be staying at Hotel Erzsebet, children will sleep in pre-arranged groups of 3. Curfew is 9.00pm. Main activities include: Budapest Opera of Bela Bartok and visiting Parliament along the Danube river. Year 6 - No field trip planned as of yet. Year 7-9 - They will be travelling to Strasbourg from Sept 9-11th. They will be led and coordinated by Mr. Basing, Mr. Woking and Mrs. Faring. They will be staying at the Hôtel Cathédrale; children will sleep in pre-arranged groups of 4. Curfew is 8.30pm. Main activities include: trip to Strasbourg Cathedral, clock maker workshop. All parents must have signed their consent forms for their child and specified dietary requirements as well as allergies.

Buildings

Birch - Classrooms for all Key Stage 2 years on 1F.  Cafeteria on GF. This allows all key stage 2 students to easily access the cafeteria via the staircase. Connected to Oak building via the 1F walkway and BF1 underpass. The BF1 underpass contains lockers for Key Stage 3 year students. Oak - Classrooms for all Key Stage 3 years except year 9 who are located in the building opposite. Ash - The Ash building has four floors. Music practice rooms are on the GF, Art suites on the 3F and the Theatre is separation from the building, equidistance from the Maple building. Maple - Located opposite Oak building, contains classrooms for one year and all administrative, financial and management offices. The reception is located on the GF.

Learning Curriculum A

All years in Key Stage 2 have twelve subjects of learning. All years in Key Stage 3 have fifteen. Sports – Physical education is an important aspect to our learning process. Our philosophy is a healthy body leads to a healthy mind. Our sport of choice is football. We compete with other schools in the local constituency. Arts – At Pinewood Academy we have music practice rooms, art suites and a theatre to allow the students to express their creative side. We boast exciting artistic opportunities throughout the year including: the annual Musical, school music concert every term, and art competitions.

Learning Curriculum B

Languages – We focus heavily on bi-lingual learning. As such, each subject is taught in either French or in English. Each student must have one third of subjects taught in French and two thirds in English. Students must determine (with discussion and consent from parents) which subjects they wish to have in French and which in English. ICT – Every class has a fully mobile interactive touch screen. ICT supports all subject areas. Each student is given a personal touch screen pad for educational purposes. Students can thus explore sensory apps, improve literacy and numeracy skills and gain important communication skills via this pad.

Organisational Structure

The Governing Board - It consists of nine elected members, one by the local council. The Board can exercise its powers of co-option; for example by inviting global organisations to nominate representatives if it so chooses, and is agreed by the Board. The Director General - The Director General is the Chief Executive and Educational Leader of Pinewood Foundation. The DG is responsible for the appointment of Principals to academies, departments and programmes. The DG is equally responsible for academic quality management, financial personnel and administrative management. In order to become a member of The Governing Board, the DG must approve the appointment. Conference of Management - The Conference is made up of all members of the Governing Board, the Director General and all senior management team in the academies; thus totaling twenty-four members. The Conference is response for formulating policies, proposals and recommendations about any matters of importance regarding the Pinewood Foundation.

questions.t: The tutor of Year 5 is Ms. Ryder.
questions.e: True - As stated in the Field Trips A tab, the tutor who leads the year for the field trip is the tutor of that year. The Year 5 field trip is led by Ms. Joy and Ms. Ryder. Thus the correct answer is true.

questions.t: The Maple building is the tallest of Pinewood’s four buildings.
questions.e: Cannot Say - As stated in the Buildings tab, while the Maple building has four floors, the total number of floors is not stated with regards to the others. Therefore, we have insufficient information. Thus the correct answer is cannot say.

questions.t: Mr. Jason’s classroom is in the Oak building.
questions.e: False - As stated in the Field Trip A tab, the tutor who leads the year for the field trip is the tutor of that year. As such, Mr. Jason is a tutor for year 4. However, as stated in the Year tab, those classes are part of Key Stage 2. In the Buildings tab, it states that the Oak building contains classrooms for Key Stage 3. The Key Stage 2 classrooms are in the Birch building. Thus the correct answer is false.

questions.t: Key Stage 3 years have the same number of subjects as Key Stage 2.
questions.n: The passage says Key Stage 3 has fifteen subjects (the explanation below misquotes fourteen). The answer is unaffected.
questions.e: False - As stated in the Learning Curriculum A tab, “all years in Key Stage 2 have twelve subjects of learning. All years in Key Stage 3 have fourteen”. Therefore, they have two more subjects and are not the same. Thus the correct answer is false.

questions.t: The Conference of Management consists of twenty-four members.
questions.e: True - As stated in the Organisational Structure tab; the conference is made up of all members of Governing Board, the DG and all senior management team -totalling twenty-four.

questions.t: Key Stage 3 student lockers are located in the Ash building.
questions.e: False - As stated in the Buildings tab, the Key Stage 3 lockers are located in the BF1 underpass. This underpass is located between the Oak and Birch buildings – not the Ash building. Thus the correct answer is false.

questions.t: The Class 5 field trip is one week following the Class 4 field trip.
questions.e: True - The class 4 field trip is on Friday 14th. The class 5 field trip is on Friday 21st. This is one week following. Thus the correct answer is true.

questions.t: Pinewood Academy won their second football on a Saturday.
questions.e: Cannot Say - While the calendar shows that the second football match was on a Saturday, there is no indication what the outcome of the match is/was. Therefore, there is insufficient information. Thus the correct answer is cannot say.

questions.t: Class 7-9 leave for Strasbourg on a Monday.
questions.e: False – As stated in the Calendar tab, they leave for Strasbourg on a Sunday, not a Monday. Thus the correct answer is false.

questions.t: Class 5 are to see a Bela Bartok opera on their field trip.
questions.e: True – As stated in the Field Trip B tab, their main activities include “Budapest Opera of Bela Bartok”. Thus the correct answer is true.

questions.t: LearnTogether Charity Fundraising will take place on 12th September, at 1pm.
questions.e: Cannot Say - It states in the Calendar tab that the LearnTogether Charity Fundraising will take place during lunch hours. While it is entirely likely that 1pm is during the lunch hours of Pinewood Academy, it is not stated as such. Therefore, we have insufficient information and cannot know the answer demonstrably either way. Thus the correct answer is cannot say.

questions.t: The main sport of Pinewood Academy is football.
questions.e: True - While the Calendar shows football matches present, it states in the Learning Curriculum A tab “our sport of choice is football”. Thus the correct answer is true.

questions.t: The local council must have a member on the Governing Board who is approved by the Director General.
questions.e: True - It states in the Organisational Structure tab that the board consists of one local council member. It also states that the DG must approve the appointment of someone becoming a member of the Governing Board. Thus the correct answer is true.

questions.t: The students go back to school for the new school year on a Tuesday.
questions.e: False – It states on the Calendar tab that the Students Return – First day of New School Year is on a Thursday, not a Tuesday. Thus the correct answer is false.

questions.t: The Governing Board can invite representatives from global organisations.
questions.e: True – It states in the Organisational Structure tab that the board can invite “global organisations to nominate representatives if it so chooses”. Thus the correct answer is true.

questions.t: At Pinewood Academy, for Key Stage 2 students, ICT is taught more in English than in French.
questions.e: Cannot Say - In the Learning Curriculum tab, it states that each subject is taught in either English or in French. While two thirds of subjects must be in English rather than French, which would indicate a likelier situation where ICT is in English rather than French, there is no indication whether the statement is true or false. We have insufficient information. Thus the correct answer is cannot say.

questions.t: At Pinewood Academy, a Key Stage 3 student is taught 6 subjects in French.
questions.e: False - In the Learning Curriculum tab, it states that Key Stage 3 students have fifteen subjects. It also states that one third of subjects must be taught in French. Therefore, they will have 5 subjects taught in French, not six. Thus the correct answer is false.

questions.t: The reception of Pinewood Academy is located in the Maple building.
questions.e: True – It states in the Buildings tab, that the reception is located on the GF of the Maple building. Thus the correct answer is true. .

questions.t: Pinewood Academy is an all-boys international school.
questions.e: False - In the Mission Statement tab, it states the Pinewood Academy is an international school for both boys and girls. Therefore, it is not an all-boys school. Thus the correct answer is false.

questions.t: The tutor of year 9 is Mrs. Faring.
questions.n: Check this one against the passage: AssessmentDay's printed explanation for this question is a copy of the one for Q19 and does not address the statement. The passage says Years 7-9 are led by Mr. Basing, Mr. Woking and Mrs. Faring but does not say which year each tutor has.
questions.e: False - In the Mission Statement tab, it states the Pinewood Academy is an international school for both boys and girls. Therefore, it is not an all-boys school. Thus the correct answer is false.

questions.t: Parents must consent to their child going on the Skywire ride.
questions.e: True - It states in the Field Trip A tab, that year 4 will have a trip to the Skywire ride which is a condition on the consent form. In Field Trip B tab, it states that parents must have signed their consent forms for their child. Therefore, parents must consent to their child going on the Skywire ride. Thus the correct answer is true.

questions.t: Year 6 will not have a Spring field trip.
questions.e: Cannot Say - In the Field Trip A tab, it states that every year there is a September trip and a Spring trip. This tab and Field Trip B tab, state the September trips but do not outline the Spring trips. Even though it states that the year 6 trip is not planned as of yet, we do not have enough information to demonstrably say that they will not have a Spring field trip. Thus the correct answer is cannot say.

questions.t: On finishing year 9, in order to take GCSEs, most students enrol at Stirling Contemporary.
questions.e: Cannot Say - The Mission Statement tab states that the sister school of Pinewood Academy which caters for GCSE’s and A-Levels. Since Pinewood Academy finishes at the end of year 9, students will need to find a new school to continue their education. Given that Stirling Contemporary is their sister school, it is likely that students would simply follow on by going there. However, there is no indication in the passages that this is the case and we have no demonstrably information to confirm either way. Thus the correct answer is cannot say.

questions.t: There are more students in Key Stage 2 years than Key Stage 3.
questions.e: Cannot Say - While Key Stage 2 has five years of students, and Key Stage 3 has three years of students, there is no direct information about what the allocation is, or whether the Key Stage 2 years have explicitly more students than Key Stage 3 years. We need more information to make it demonstrably true or false. Thus the correct answer is cannot say.

questions.t: On the field trip to Budapest, children will sleep in groups of four.
questions.e: False - It states in the Field Trip B tab, on the Year 5 field trip that are going to Budapest, that children will sleep in “pre-arranged groups of three”. Not to be confused with the groups of four for the Strasbourg trip. Thus the correct answer is false.

questions.t: Years 7 and 8 can get from their classroom to the cafeteria from without going through the GF entrance of the Oak building.
questions.e: True - In the Buildings tab, it states that Key Stage 3 years, except year 9 (which indicates years 7 and 8) have classrooms in the Oak building. It also states that the Birch building houses the cafeteria on the GF which is connected to the Oak building via a walkway on 1F. Also, there is a staircase on 1F of the Birch building which takes students directly to the cafeteria. Therefore, year 7 and 8 students can walk from their classroom, across the 1F walkway to the Birch building, and down the staircase to the cafeteria without having to go through the GF entrance of the Oak building. Thus the correct answer is true.

questions.t: At Pinewood Academy, the art suites are on the 2F of the Ash building.
questions.e: False - In the Buildings tab, it states that the art suites are on the 3F of the Ash building, not the 2F. Thus the correct answer is false.

questions.t: At Pinewood Academy, the annual Musical is held in April.
questions.e: Cannot Say - In the Learning Curriculum A tab, it states that there is an annual musical. However, it does not state when that musical takes place, nor is there any other mention of it. Therefore, we have insufficient information. Thus the correct answer is cannot say.

questions.t: At Pinewood Academy, Year 5 students are ages 9-10.
questions.e: True – In the Years tab, it states that those in Year 5 are ages 9-10. Therefore, this is demonstrably true given the information available. Thus the correct answer is true.

questions.e: True - In the Learning Curriculum B tab, it states under the ICT heading that indeed, “each student is given a personal touch screen pad”. Thus the correct answer is true.

In the Calendar tab, on the 7th September it states that Pinewood Academy will be competing against Crampton School at football. Therefore, given the logical inductive from the information at hand, this statement is true. Thus the correct answer is true.
